# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll explore the codebase to locate the enrichment/categorization logic and the fixtures behind these RC 2.14 regressions.

# Transaction Categorization / Enrichment — Codebase Report

## 1. Overall project structure

**Stack:** Python 3.9 Flask microservice (`categorizationapp`), served by gunicorn on port **9898**.

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/Dockerfile` | Builds image, `pip install -e .`, runs gunicorn |
| `/app/categorizationapp/setup.py` | Package deps: Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scikit-learn, etc. |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` | Flask app bootstrap |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | HTTP API + bank dispatch |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | **35 bank-specific** categorize functions |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/` | Shared enrichment pipeline |

**No tests, fixtures, baselines, README, or sample payloads exist in this repo.** Single git commit: `047782b import codebase` (2026-07-15). File mtimes show only `Canara.py` and `PNB.py` as “recently touched” relative to others (same import commit otherwise).

### How enrichment works (pipeline)

For each bank, `POST /categorizeTransaction` runs the same chain:

```
clean_input_df
  → categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)   # category + partyName + subcategory seeds
  → [if CREDIT_CARD] card_clean_names → card_purpose
  → purpose(transactions, accountType)                          # subcategory / purpose overrides; can re-set category
  → clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)                # merchant canonicalization
  → [if accountHolder] internal_payment(...)
  → [if SAVING] salary_detection(...)
  → [if isPFMEnabled] pfm_categorization → simple_description
  → JSON response
```

**Key API** (`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`):

- `POST /categorizeTransaction` — main enrichment
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` — recurrence helper
- `GET /` — health

**Request fields:** `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `transactions[]`, optional `isPFMEnabled`.

**Per-bank script pattern** (all BankScripts):

1. Ordered `np.select` rules → `transactionCategory` (default **`"TRANSFER"`**)
2. Optional subcategory / merchantType rules
3. Ordered `np.select` rules → `partyName` from `description` / `remark` (slash/dash/colon splitters)
4. Cleanup pass on `partyName`
5. `party2` = spaceless `partyName` for fuzzy matching

**Helpers** (`AppUtil.py`): `sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_colon`, `py_extract`, `fuzzy_match`.

**Shared regex catalogs:**

- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` — bank-specific cheque/UPI/NEFT/verification patterns  
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` — merchant/purpose dictionaries (loans, P2P NBFCs, salary, etc.)

**Output enums:**

- Categories: `TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (includes `CHEQUE_PAID`, `TRANSFER`, `UPI`, `IMPS`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, …)
- Subcategories: `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py`

---

## 2. Where categories and counterparty names come from

### Category

Derived **only from statement narration** (`description`) and sometimes `remark`, `amount`, `type`, via first-match `np.select` in each bank script. Unmatched → **`TRANSFER`**.

### Counterparty (`partyName`)

Also narration-driven:

- Split on `/`, `-`, `:`, `~`, `*`, `_`
- Capture groups via `py_extract`
- Post-filters strip refs, “NA”, bank tags, pure digits
- Then global `clean_names()` maps party strings to canonical merchants (huge rule list ~1971 lines)

### Purpose / subcategory

`Purpose.py` overlays purpose (salary, loan repayment, fuel, etc.) using party + description + category. Also:

- `amount ∈ {1,-1}` + subcategory LOAN → **`ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`** (line 165)
- Clears subcategory for categories matching `VERIFICATION|CHARGES|BOUNCE|...`

---

## 3. Test fixtures / baselines

| Item | Status |
|------|--------|
| Unit/integration tests | **None** |
| Fixture JSON/CSV | **None** (`.csv` is gitignored) |
| Baseline/expected labels | **None** |
| Regression harness | **None** |

There is nothing in-repo related to cheques, transfers, UPI, or account-verification test cases.

### How you would run / exercise this

```bash
# Install & run service
cd /app/categorizationapp
pip3 install -e .
# or via Docker from /app
docker build -t txn-enrichment .
docker run -p 9898:9898 txn-enrichment

# Smoke call
curl -X POST http://localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "bank": "HDFC",
    "acc_type": "SAVING",
    "accountUID": "test",
    "accountHolder": "",
    "transactions": [{
      "description": "CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR",
      "amount": 5000,
      "type": "DEBIT",
      "remark": "",
      "balanceAfterTransaction": 10000,
      "transactionDate": "2024-01-01"
    }]
  }'
```

**Bank codes** used in Controller include: `HDFC`, `ICICI`, `SBI`, `PNB`, `CANARA`, `AXIS`, `KOTAK`, `YES_BANK`, `IDFC`, `IDBI`, `BOB`, `BOI`, `UNION_BANK`, `INDUSIND`, `BANK_OF_MAHARASHTRA`, `PAYTM`, `RBL`, `CITI`, `STANDARD_CHARTERED`, `FEDERAL`, `CENTRAL_BANK`, `ANDHRA_BANK`, `SYNDICATE`, `KARNATAKA`, `KARUR_VYASA`, `CITY_UNION`, `AU_SMALL_FINANCE`, `BANDHAN`, `INDIAN`, `SOUTH_INDIAN`, `SARASWAT`, `SVC_BANK`, `TAMILNAD_MERCANTILE`, `UCO`, `DCB`, etc. Unknown bank → `"Bank Not Found."`

Ad-hoc regression would mean calling the API (or importing `categorize_*` functions) with fixed narrations and asserting `transactionCategory` / `partyName`.

---

## 4. Code paths mapped to QA findings F-1 … F-5

### F-1: Cheque debit with bare number note → generic `TRANSFER`

**Root cause:** Default category is always `"TRANSFER"`. Cheque is only set when narration/remark matches bank-specific patterns. A bare cheque number with no `CHQ`/`CLG` keyword often never matches.

**Banks that *do* treat numeric remarks as cheque:**

| Bank | File | Rule |
|------|------|------|
| PNB | `BankScripts/PNB.py:60-61` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{5}$` DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; 5–6 digits CREDIT → deposit |
| Axis | `Axis.py:58-59` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| Kotak | `Kotak.py:65-67` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,5}$` |
| YES | `YES.py:52-53` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,6}$` |
| UCO | `UCO.py:44-45` | same |
| RBL | `RBL.py:49-50` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$` only |
| HDFC | `HDFC.py:100` | **CREDIT only**: 16-char remark `0{11}[0-9]{5}` → deposit; **no bare-number debit rule** |

**Banks weak on bare-number cheques:** Canara (`Canara.py:70-71` needs `chq|clg|cheque`), SBI (`SBI.py:45-46` needs CLG/CHQ), ICICI (`ICICI.py:69-72` needs CLG or remark containing `"CHEQUE"`), HDFC debit side.

**PNB special case:** `PNB_CHQ_0 = "^TO TRF? -\\s?[0-9]+$"` forces **empty** partyName for bare “TO TRF - 123456” (`PNB.py:123`, `BankRegexConstants.py:140`). Category may still be TRANSFER if remark is empty and description has no CLG keyword.

**Relevant defaults:** every bank ends with  
`np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`.

---

### F-2: `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty = clearing tag, not name

**Strongest smoking gun — Canara:**

```165:166:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
[transactions.description.str.contains("^CHQ PAID-", ...), sep_by_dash(...,1,2)],
```

For `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`:

- split `-` → `["CHQ PAID", "MICR CLG", "RAVI KUMAR"]`
- index **1** → **`"MICR CLG"`** (internal clearing tag)
- correct name is index **2** → `"RAVI KUMAR"`

Compare neighboring rule for home clearing which *does* use index 2:

```164:164:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
[... "Chq Paid-Home Clearing-", ... sep_by_dash(...,2,3)],
```

**HDFC path for same narration:**

| Step | Location | Behavior |
|------|----------|----------|
| Category | `HDFC.py:71-74` | `\bCHQ\b` / `Chq Paid` → `CHEQUE_PAID` |
| Name extract | `HDFC.py:163` | Any `CHQ PAID-` → `sep_by_dash(3,4)` → **empty** (only 3 segments) |
| Name extract | `BankRegexConstants.py:86` `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` | Only `MICR CTS`, **not** `MICR CLG` |
| Cleanup | `HDFC.py:260` | `Micr Clg\|Chq Paid` → blank partyName |

So HDFC either blanks the name or never grabs “RAVI KUMAR”; Canara actively sets party to **MICR CLG**.

**Patterns to fix:**

- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:80-90` (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*`)
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py:163,187-197,260`
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py:163-166`

---

### F-3: Inbound electronic-transfer credits with blank counterparty

Party extraction is format-specific; wrong slash/dash index or post-filters wipe names.

**High-risk cleanup that blanks names:**

| Location | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `ICICI.py:233` | party with `[0-9]{6,}` → `""` (except CMS/IFT) |
| `Canara.py:174` | party matching `^[0-9]{5,}` → `""` |
| `HDFC.py:261` | party with no letters → `""` |
| `HDFC.py:226` | NEFT party matching long numeric pattern → `""` |
| `SBI.py:174-176` | IMPS party starting with Transfer/Imps/Remitter/Remarks → `""` |
| `RBL.py:137` | `^[0-9]{7,}` and similar → `""` |
| `Karnataka.py:92` | `^[0-9]{2,}` → `""` |

**Inbound credit extractors (examples):**

- **ICICI IMPS/NEFT:** `ICICI.py:163-167` — `MMT/IMPS` uses slash index 3 or 4; easy to land on UTR/ref instead of name, then digit filter blanks it  
- **HDFC IMPS/NEFT:** `HDFC.py:155-162` — dash-split index 2; formats without enough dashes → empty  
- **SBI NEFT:** `SBI.py:120-122` — star-split + digit strip can erase names that are mostly numeric refs  
- **PNB NEFT IN:** `PNB.py:97-110` — many format variants; unlisted formats stay blank  
- **Canara NEFT/IMPS credit:** `Canara.py:117-127` — `IMPS-CREDIT` dash split; `IMPS:` colon split  

**Generic TRANSFER name fallbacks** only fire when description is “clean letters” (no digits/punctuation), e.g. `PNB.py:161`, `HDFC.py:214-215`, `Canara.py:158` — typical bank transfer narrations with UTRs fail these and stay blank.

---

### F-4: P2P instant-payment credit showing bare reference as name

UPI/IMPS party often taken from the wrong slash field (UTR / RRN / txn id).

| Bank | Extract | Risk |
|------|---------|------|
| SBI | `SBI.py:99` `UPI` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)` | Field 3 is often RRN/ref on some SBI layouts |
| HDFC | `HDFC.py:154` `^UPI-` → dash index 1; then `227` if party has 9–15 digits, retry index 2 | Partial mitigation only |
| PNB | `PNB.py:152-156` P2M/P2A/P2V slash indices | P2A index 4 can be ref; cleanup `177` only clears `Na|Tr|Chq` not pure numbers |
| Axis | `Axis.py:122` UPI/IMPS → slash index 3 | Common UPI RRN position |
| Canara | `Canara.py:107-109` UPI slash indices | Then `174` blanks `^[0-9]{5,}` — good for pure-numeric, fails if ref is mixed/wrong field kept as “name” |
| ICICI | `ICICI.py:211` UPI Razorpay special-case; general UPI earlier in file | Digit wipe at 233 |

**Purpose.py** `P2P` (`RegexConstants.py:115`) is **merchantType “P2P NBFC”** (lendbox, monexo, etc.), **not** UPI P2P person-to-person. Unrelated to F-4 naming.

---

### F-5: Account verification / token deposit → `TRANSFER` not `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`

**Clear bugs:**

1. **Canara amount threshold is wrong**

```19:19:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
... BANK_VERIF ... & transactions.amount.lt(1) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"
```

`amount.lt(1)` is **amount < 1**. A classic **₹1** penny-drop **never matches**. Other banks use `.lt(2)`, `.eq(1)`, or `.isin([1,-1])`.

2. **String vs numeric amount (never matches after `clean_input_df`)**

`AppUtil.clean_input_df` does `pd.to_numeric(amount)`.

But:

- `BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37` — `amount.isin(["1","-1"])` and `isin(["1"])` **strings**
- `Indusind.py:29,31` — same string `"1"` / `"-1"`

Numeric `1.0` ∉ `{"1"}` → verification rules dead; falls through to **TRANSFER** (or IMPS/UPI if those keywords present).

3. **Banks with no ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION at all**

`Bandhan`, `Citi`, `CityUnion`, `DCB`, `Federal`, `Indian`, `KarurVyasa`, `SVC`, `Saraswat`, `UCO`.

4. **Narrow / incomplete keyword sets**

| Bank | Constant / rule | Gap |
|------|-----------------|-----|
| PNB | `ACC_VERIFY_PNB = "A/C VALIDATION\|BE NE NAME\|ACC VALI"` | Very narrow; misses pennydrop/verif/BAV |
| Kotak | Only `Karz Xx4002` and `^Received from [A-Z]` + amount 1 | Misses generic penny drops |
| YES | `Acc validation` only + amount.eq(1) | Narrow |
| HDFC | Uses `BANK_VER` (Axis set), **not** unused `BANK_VER_HD` which includes `"ACCOUNT VERIFICATION"` | `BANK_VER_HD` defined `BankRegexConstants.py:75` but HDFC imports/`uses` `BANK_VER` line 13 |
| Canara | `BANK_VERIF` includes broad `FUND TRANS\|IMPS Txn` but broken by `.lt(1)` | Would over-fire if threshold fixed without tightening |

5. **Purpose-layer safety net only for LOAN subcategory**

`Purpose.py:165`: LOAN + amount ±1 → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION. Does **not** catch generic IMPS/UPI ₹1 credits already labeled TRANSFER/IMPS/UPI.

6. **Axis is aggressive (contrast)**

`Axis.py:26`: **any CREDIT amount == 1** → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION (plus keyword and mandate rules).

---

## 5. Key functions & files (quick index)

| Function | File |
|----------|------|
| `categorizeTransaction` | `Controller.py:69` |
| `categorize_*_transactions` | `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` |
| `purpose` | `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` |
| `clean_names` | `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` |
| `internal_payment` | `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` |
| `salary_detection` | `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` |
| `pfm_categorization` / `simple_description` | `PFMCategorization.py` / `SimpleDescription.py` |
| `clean_input_df`, separators, `py_extract` | `AppUtil.py` |
| Category/subcategory display values | `TransactionCategoryEnums.py`, `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` |
| Cheque/verification regexes | `BankRegexConstants.py` |
| Merchant/purpose dictionaries | `RegexConstants.py` |

---

## 6. Patterns that look broken or inconsistent (summary)

| Issue | Where | Why it matters |
|-------|-------|----------------|
| Canara `amount.lt(1)` for verification | `Canara.py:19` | ₹1 token deposits → TRANSFER (**F-5**) |
| BOM/Indusind string amounts | `BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37`, `Indusind.py:29-31` | Rules never fire after numeric cast (**F-5**) |
| Canara `^CHQ PAID-` → dash index 1 | `Canara.py:165` | partyName = `MICR CLG` not payee (**F-2**) |
| HDFC `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` only `MICR CTS` | `BankRegexConstants.py:86` | `MICR CLG` name path missing (**F-2**) |
| HDFC `CHQ PAID-` uses dash index 3 | `HDFC.py:163` | Wrong for short `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-NAME` (**F-2**) |
| HDFC blanks `Micr Clg` party | `HDFC.py:260` | Clears tag but doesn’t recover name |
| Default category TRANSFER | all BankScripts | Bare cheque notes without keywords → TRANSFER (**F-1**) |
| HDFC no bare-number debit cheque | `HDFC.py` | Same as F-1 for numeric-only notes |
| Digit-only / long-digit party wipe | ICICI/Canara/HDFC/RBL/… | Blank counterparty on electronic credits (**F-3**) |
| UPI slash-index heuristics | SBI/Axis/PNB/HDFC | RRN/ref as partyName (**F-4**) |
| `BANK_VER_HD` unused | `BankRegexConstants.py:75` vs `HDFC.py:13` | Stronger verification regex never applied |
| No automated tests | whole repo | No baseline to catch F-1…F-5 regressions |
| Purpose LOAN±1 only | `Purpose.py:165` | Incomplete global verification backstop |

---

## 7. Suggested fix / test focus (for implementers)

There is no existing fixture harness; recommended minimal regression set (call `/categorizeTransaction` or unit-import bank functions):

1. **F-1:** DEBIT, description/remark = bare cheque number only (per bank formats), expect `CHEQUE_PAID` not `TRANSFER`.  
2. **F-2:** `"CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR"` DEBIT on **Canara** and **HDFC**, expect category `CHEQUE_PAID`, partyName containing `Ravi Kumar` not `Micr Clg`.  
3. **F-3:** Sample inbound NEFT/IMPS credits with standard bank layouts; expect non-empty human partyName.  
4. **F-4:** UPI P2P credit narrations where middle field is RRN; expect name field, not bare reference.  
5. **F-5:** amount `1` CREDIT with penny-drop / validation keywords (and Canara `IMPS`/`FUND TRANS` cases); expect `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`; also BOM/Indusind after fixing type comparison.

**Highest-confidence code defects for the five findings:** `Canara.py:19` (F-5), `Canara.py:165` (F-2), BOM/Indusind string amounts (F-5), HDFC cheque MICR CLG gap (F-2), universal TRANSFER default + missing bare-cheque rules (F-1).
</task_result>
